Network — Both sides of the marketplace
12–24 months · $1M–$8M ARR
VCs subscribe for deal-flow filtering. Operators list profiles. Service providers (legal, accounting, market entry) onboard. Each new participant compounds value for the others — classic network effects.
Target metric: 5K founders × 200 VCs × 500 operators on platform
03
Private data — The actual moat
24–36 months · $8M–$30M ARR
Founders share KPIs (ARR, retention, NDR, comp) in exchange for personalized matches. After 24 months, you have proprietary benchmarks no public dataset can match. This is what PitchBook charges $30K/seat for.
Target metric: 10K companies sharing live KPIs · 500 cohorts indexed
04
Distribution — Embedded everywhere
36–48 months · $30M–$80M ARR
Atlas API powers benchmark widgets in CRM tools, finance software, accelerator stacks. Every B2B SaaS targeting startups embeds Atlas data. You become infrastructure.
Target metric: 50 SaaS API customers · 100M API calls/month
05
Outcome rail — Where capital actually flows
48–60 months · $80M–$200M ARR
Atlas becomes the rail VCs trust for due diligence, founders trust for fundraising prep, corporates trust for M&A scouting. 10–15× revenue multiple at growth → $1B–$3B valuation.
Unicorn checkpoint: $100M ARR, 35% YoY growth, 90%+ NRR
◈ WHAT THIS PLAN DOES NOT ASSUME
  • It does not assume we out-scale PitchBook/Crunchbase on dataset size — we don't, and we shouldn't try.
  • It does not assume "AI predicts unicorns" — that pitch loses credibility in 30 seconds with sophisticated investors.
  • It does not assume one ₹100Cr report sells — instead, $99–$15K products at scale add up to $100M ARR.
  • It does not assume India alone — global addressable market for founder decision tools is the unlock.

What it does assume: that the right combination of habit-forming workflow, two-sided network, and proprietary KPI data — built patiently over 4–5 years — produces a category-defining company. That has happened many times. Stripe did it for payments. Notion did it for docs. Atlas can do it for growth decisions.
